newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel favours selling banks in share offering.
newsitem.headline: Israel favours selling banks in share offering.

text.p: The prime minister's office favours privatising Israel's state-controlled banks through public share offerings rather than by selling controlling stakes to strategic investors, a source in the prime minister's office said.
Israel has failed so far in its attempts to sell controlling stakes in Hapoalim and Leumi, the country's two largest banks, to strategic investors.
The prime minister's office is currently preparing a four-year privatisation programme that will be submitted to the government in October or November.
Since taking office, Prime Minster Benjamin Netanyahu has moved the Government Corporations Authority, which overseas privatisation, from the Treasury to his office.
The plans call for raising about $6 billion shekels from privatisation in 1996, the source in the prime minister's office said.
